  sumPiEquivProdPi (fun b ↦ α (e b)) |>.symm.trans (.piCongrLeft (fun i : ↥(s ∪ t) ↦ α i) e)

English
Let $I$ be a set. Let $x_{1}$ be a function from elements of $I$ to sets. Let $s$ and $t$ be finite sets of $I$ such that $s$ is disjoint to $t$. Let $f$ be a function from elements $i_{6}$ of $\SubtypeSet {x_{21}}{(\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{x_{21}})}$ to elements of $x_{1} (i_{6})$. Let $g$ be a function from elements $i_{5}$ of $\SubtypeSet {x_{19}}{(\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {t}{x_{19}})}$ to elements of $x_{1} (i_{5})$. Let $i \in I$ such that $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {s}{i}$ and $\MembershipmemMACRoDQ {\UnionunionMACRoDY {s}{t}}{i}$. Then $\operatorname{piFinsetUnion} (x_{1} , h , \ProdmkMACRoDR {f}{g}, i (\mathrm{hi'}))$ is equal to $f (i (\mathrm{hi}))$.

lemma piFinsetUnion_right {ι} [DecidableEq ι] (α : ι → Type*) {s t : Finset ι}
    (h : Disjoint s t) {f g} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ t) (hi' : i ∈ s ∪ t) :
    Equiv.piFinsetUnion α h (f, g) ⟨i, hi'⟩ = g ⟨i, hi⟩ := by
  simp_rw [piFinsetUnion, sumPiEquivProdPi, piCongrLeft, piCongrLeft', trans_apply, coe_fn_symm_mk]
  rw! [Finset.union_symm_right h hi hi']
  rfl

English
Let $X$ be a set. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $P$ be a function from elements of $X$ to propositions. Let $n \in \Natural$. Then $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {(\FinsetFilter {x_{1}}{P (x_{1})}{s})}\leq n$, if and only if for all finite sets $s'$ of $X$, if $s'$ is a subset of $s$, then if $n < \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s'}$, then there exists an element $a$ of $X$, such that $a$ is an element of $s'$ and it is not the case that $P (a)$.
French
Soit $X$ un ensemble. Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $X$. Soit $P$ une fonction des éléments de $X$ à des propositions. Soit $n \in \Natural$. Alors $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {(\FinsetFilter {x_{1}}{P (x_{1})}{s})}\leq n$ si et seulement si pour tous les ensembles finis $s'$ de $X$, si $\SetSubsetMACRoFR {s'}{s}$, alors si $n < \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s'}$, alors il existe un élément $a$ de $X$ tel que $a$ soit un élément de $s'$ et il ne soit pas le cas que $P (a)$.
Czech
Nechť $X$ je množina. Nechť $s$ je konečná množina $X$. Nechť $P$ je funkce z prvků z $X$ do výroků. Nechť $n \in \Natural$. Tedy $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {(\FinsetFilter {x_{1}}{P (x_{1})}{s})}\leq n$, právě tehdy, když pro všechny konečné množiny $s'$ $X$, jestliže $s'$ je podmnožina $s$, pak jestliže $n < \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s'}$, pak existuje prvek $a$ z $X$, takový, že $a$ je element $s'$ a není případ že $P (a)$.
Formula
$X \in \mathrm{Set} , s \in \mathrm{Finset} (X), P \in X \rightarrow \mathrm{Prop} , n \in \Natural \vdash \FinsetcardMACRoDQ {(\FinsetFilter {x_{1}}{P (x_{1})}{s})}\leq n \leftrightarrow (\forall s' \in \mathrm{Finset} (X). \SetSubsetMACRoGA {s'}{s}\rightarrow n < \FinsetcardMACRoDQ {s'}\rightarrow (\exists a \in X . \MembershipmemMACRoDX {s'}{a}\wedge \neg P (a)))$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Let $f$ be an embedding of $X$ and $Y$. Then the cardinality of the map of $f$ and $s$ is equal to the cardinality of $s$.

Finset.card_bijtheoremCard.lean:356
Given a bijection from a finite set s to a finite set t, the cardinalities of s and t are equal.
The difference with Finset.card_bij' is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection, rather than by an inverse function.
The difference with Finset.card_nbij is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the domain, rather than being a non-dependent function.
Lean
lemma card_bij (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t)
    (i_inj : ∀ a₁ ha₁ a₂ ha₂, i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂)
    (i_surj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, i a ha = b) : #s = #t := by
  classical
  calc
    #s = #s.attach := card_attach.symm
    _ = #(s.attach.image fun a ↦ i a.1 a.2) := Eq.symm ?_
    _ = #t := ?_
  · apply card_image_of_injective
    intro ⟨_, _⟩ ⟨_, _⟩ h
    simpa using i_inj _ _ _ _ h
  · congr 1
    ext b
    constructor <;> intro h
    · obtain ⟨_, _, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 h; apply hi
    · obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := i_surj b h; exact mem_image.2 ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, by simp⟩

Alors $\FinsetcardMACRoDJ {s}= \FinsetcardMACRoDJ {t}$.

Finset.card_bij'theoremCard.lean:381
Given a bijection from a finite set s to a finite set t, the cardinalities of s and t are equal.
The difference with Finset.card_bij is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather than as a surjective injection.
The difference with Finset.card_nbij' is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use membership of the domains, rather than being non-dependent functions.
Lean
lemma card_bij' (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (j : ∀ a ∈ t, α) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t)
    (hj : ∀ a ha, j a ha ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ha, j (i a ha) (hi a ha) = a)
    (right_inv : ∀ a ha, i (j a ha) (hj a ha) = a) : #s = #t := by
  refine card_bij i hi (fun a1 h1 a2 h2 eq ↦ ?_) (fun b hb ↦ ⟨_, hj b hb, right_inv b hb⟩)
  rw [← left_inv a1 h1, ← left_inv a2 h2]
  simp only [eq]

Given a bijection from a finite set s to a finite set t, the cardinalities of s and t are equal.
The difference with Finset.card_nbij' is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection, rather than by an inverse function.
The difference with Finset.card_bij is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domain.

The difference with Finset.card_nbij is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather than as a surjective injection.
The difference with Finset.card_bij' is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains.

Finset.strongInductiondefCard.lean:857
Suppose that, given objects defined on all strict subsets of any finset s, one knows how to define an object on s. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets, starting from the empty set and iterating. This can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.
Lean
def strongInduction {p : Finset α → Sort*} (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s) :
    ∀ s : Finset α, p s
  | s =>
    H s fun t h =>
      have : #t < #s := card_lt_card h
      strongInduction H t
  termination_by s => #s

Let $X$ be a set. Let $p$ be a function from finite sets of $X$ to sets. Let $H$ be a function from finite sets $s_{1}$ of $X$ and functions from finite sets $t_{1}$ of $X$ and elements of $\mathrm{Proof} (\HasSSubsetSSubsetMACRoFS {t_{1}}{s_{1}})$ to elements of $p (t_{1})$ to elements of $p (s_{1})$. Let $s$ be a finite set of $X$. Then the strong induction of $H$ and $s$ is equal to $H$ applied to $s$ and the function that maps $t$ and $h$ to the strong induction of $H$ and $t$.

Soit $s$ un ensemble fini de $X$. Alors l'induction forte de $H$ et $s$ est égale à $H$ appliqué à $s$ et la fonction qui envoie $t$ et $h$ sur l'induction forte de $H$ et $t$.

Suppose that, given objects defined on all nonempty strict subsets of any nontrivial finset s, one knows how to define an object on s. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets, starting from singletons and iterating.
TODO: Currently this can only be used to prove properties. Replace Finset.Nonempty.exists_eq_singleton_or_nontrivial with computational content in order to let p be Sort-valued.

@[elab_as_elim]
protected lemma Nonempty.strong_induction {p : ∀ s, s.Nonempty → Prop}
    (h₀ : ∀ a, p {a} (singleton_nonempty _))
    (h₁ : ∀ ⦃s⦄ (hs : s.Nontrivial), (∀ t ht, t ⊂ s → p t ht) → p s hs.nonempty) :
    ∀ ⦃s : Finset α⦄ (hs), p s hs
  | s, hs => by
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ | hs := hs.exists_eq_singleton_or_nontrivial
    · exact h₀ _
    · refine h₁ hs fun t ht hts ↦ ?_
      have := card_lt_card hts
      exact ht.strong_induction h₀ h₁
termination_by s => #s

Finset.strongDownwardInductiondefCard.lean:911
Suppose that, given that p t can be defined on all supersets of s of cardinality less than n, one knows how to define p s. Then one can inductively define p s for all finsets s of cardinality less than n, starting from finsets of card n and iterating. This can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.
Lean
def strongDownwardInduction {p : Finset α → Sort*} {n : ℕ}
    (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁) :
    ∀ s : Finset α, #s ≤ n → p s
  | s =>
    H s fun {t} ht h =>
      have := Finset.card_lt_card h
      have : n - #t < n - #s := by lia
      strongDownwardInduction H t ht
  termination_by s => n - #s

Finset.eraseInductiontheoremCard.lean:954
To prove a proposition for an arbitrary Finset α, it suffices to prove that for any S : Finset α, the following is true: the property is true for S with any element s removed, then the property holds for S.
This is a weaker version of Finset.strongInduction. But it can be more precise when the induction argument only requires removing single elements at a time.
Lean
theorem eraseInduction [DecidableEq α] {p : Finset α → Prop}
    (H : (S : Finset α) → (∀ s ∈ S, p (S.erase s)) → p S) (S : Finset α) : p S :=
  S.strongInduction fun S ih => H S fun _ hs => ih _ (erase_ssubset hs)

Finset.image_iterate_stabilises_lt_cardtheoremCard.lean:963
Given a function f which sends the finite set s to itself, the sequence of images of s under iterates of f is eventually constant. Furthermore, the sequence of images stabilises in fewer than #s steps.
Lean
theorem image_iterate_stabilises_lt_card [DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {s : Finset α}
    (hs : Set.MapsTo f s s) (hs₀ : s.Nonempty) :
    ∃ n < #s, ∀ m, n ≤ m → s.image f^[m] = s.image f^[n] := by
  let g (i : ℕ) : Finset α := s.image f^[i]
  have (i : ℕ) : 0 < #(g i) := (hs₀.image _).card_pos
  have hg : Antitone g := antitone_nat_of_succ_le <| fun i ↦ by
    simp_rw [g, Function.iterate_succ, ← image_image]
    grw [hs.finsetImage_subset]
  have eq_iff (i j : ℕ) : #(g i) - 1 = #(g j) - 1 ↔ g i = g j := by
    wlog hij : j ≤ i generalizing i j
    · grind
    exact ⟨fun h ↦ eq_of_subset_of_card_le (hg hij) (by grind), by grind⟩
  have hG : Antitone (fun i ↦ #(g i) - 1) := fun i j h ↦ by dsimp; gcongr #?_ - 1; exact hg h
  rcases Nat.stabilises_of_antitone hG (by grind [=_ image_image, iterate_succ']) with ⟨n, hn, hn'⟩
  exact ⟨n, by grind⟩

Given a function f which sends the finite set s to itself, the sequence of images of s under iterates of f is eventually constant. Furthermore, the sequence of images stabilises in at most #s steps.
Lean
theorem image_iterate_stabilises_le_card [DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {s : Finset α}
    (hs : Set.MapsTo f s s) :
    ∃ n ≤ #s, ∀ m, n ≤ m → s.image f^[m] = s.image f^[n] := by
  obtain rfl | hs₀ := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · simp
  obtain ⟨n, hn', hn⟩ := image_iterate_stabilises_lt_card hs hs₀
  exact ⟨n, hn'.le, hn⟩
